question: Refer to the apparatus diagram shown. Which explanation correctly identifies the collection method and the reason for using it?

      <!-- Delivery tube entering jar -->
      <path d="M 80 50 L 170 50 L 170 145" fill="none" stroke="#64748b" stroke-width="3"/>

      <g transform="translate(150, 45)">

        <rect x="2" y="55" width="41" height="53" fill="#fef08a" opacity="0.5"/>
        <text x="22" y="85" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="800" fill="#854d0e">HCl Gas</text>
      </g>
      <!-- Displaced Air Arrow -->
      <defs>
        <marker id="arrAir" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="5" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
          <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="#3b82f6"/>
        </marker>
      </defs>
      <path d="M 185 60 Q 210 35 230 45" fill="none" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#arrAir)"/>
      <text x="250" y="45" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#2563eb">Air displaced upwards ↑</text>
      <!-- Explanatory Box -->
      <rect x="230" y="70" width="200" height="85" rx="5" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#bfdbfe"/>
      <text x="330" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#1e40af">Why This Method?</text>
      <text x="240" y="112" font-size="9.5" fill="#334155">• HCl Vapour Density = 18.25</text>
      <text x="240" y="127" font-size="9.5" fill="#334155">• Air Vapour Density = 14.4</text>
      <text x="240" y="142" font-size="9.5" font-weight="600" fill="#dc2626">• Cannot collect over water (Highly soluble!)</text>
      <text x="230" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="#475569">HCl is 1.28 times denser than air and settles at the bottom of an upright jar</text>

options.text: Downward delivery because HCl is lighter than air and practically insoluble in water.
Collection over water because HCl does not support combustion.
Upward delivery because HCl is lighter than air, although it dissolves readily in water.
Upward delivery, or downward displacement of air, because HCl is heavier than air; it cannot conveniently be collected over water because it is extremely soluble in water.

explanation:
The vapour density of HCl is 18.25, and the gas is heavier than air. Therefore, it is collected by downward displacement of air, also called upward delivery. Its solubility—about 450 volumes of HCl per volume of water—rules out collection over water. Option C identifies the method but reverses the density relationship.

      <rect x="250" y="108" width="170" height="36" rx="3" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#fca5a5"/>
      <text x="335" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9.5" font-weight="700" fill="#7f1d1d">CaO + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O</text>

options.text: Quicklime reacts with the acidic HCl gas, whereas concentrated H₂SO₄ is the specified drying agent.
Quicklime makes HCl lighter than air and changes its vapour density.
Quicklime is too volatile to remain in a drying bottle.
Quicklime converts all the HCl gas into hydrogen and chlorine.

explanation:
A suitable drying agent must remove moisture without consuming the gas being dried. Quicklime is a basic oxide and reacts with acidic HCl. Concentrated H₂SO₄ is used to dry HCl gas. Option B incorrectly attributes a change in density to the drying agent.

title: Inverted-funnel arrangement
question: Refer to the apparatus diagram shown. Why is the rim of the inverted funnel positioned just at the water surface rather than being immersed deeply in the water?

      <text x="245" y="112" font-size="9" fill="#475569">If water rises, rim lifts above surface;</text>
      <text x="245" y="124" font-size="9" fill="#475569">air enters and water drops back.</text>
      <text x="235" y="142" font-size="9.5" font-weight="700" fill="#0f172a">2. Large Surface Area:</text>

options.text: To stop HCl from dissolving in water until the gas jar is full.
To collect HCl by upward displacement of air inside the beaker.
To permit rapid absorption of highly soluble HCl while helping prevent back suction of water into the gas-generating apparatus.
To prevent hydrochloric acid from forming when HCl contacts water.

explanation:
HCl is extremely soluble in water. The inverted funnel provides a large contact area for absorption, and its rim just touching the water surface helps reduce the risk of back suction. Option A contradicts the purpose of the arrangement: the aim is to absorb HCl rapidly.

question: A student prepares HCl by heating NaCl with concentrated H₂SO₄ below 200°C, dries the gas with concentrated H₂SO₄, collects it by upward delivery, and then dissolves a portion in water. The aqueous solution is tested with blue litmus and AgNO₃. Which sequence of conclusions is entirely correct?

options.text: Na₂SO₄ forms in the first stage; HCl is collected over water; dry blue litmus turns red; AgNO₃ gives a black precipitate.
NaHSO₄ forms in the first stage; HCl is lighter than air; aqueous blue litmus remains blue; AgCl dissolves in dilute HNO₃.
NaHSO₄ forms in the first stage; HCl is dried with quicklime; dry blue litmus turns red; AgNO₃ produces PbCl₂.

explanation:
The first-stage reaction is


NaCl+H_2SO₄(conc.)→ NaHSO₄+HCl


Concentrated H₂SO₄ dries HCl, which is collected by upward delivery because it is heavier than air. Dry HCl does not turn dry blue litmus red, but aqueous HCl does. Silver nitrate produces white curdy AgCl, insoluble in dilute HNO₃. Option C uses an unsuitable drying agent and incorrectly predicts the litmus result.
